decisions.reason: NL2's requirement quote calls for disjoint conditions distinguishing the two alternatives. The exact inspection facts show transition:line:87 and transition:line:88 use distinct triggers (high_way_true, urban_way_true) rather than guard expressions, so no guard fact in the closed model certifies mutual exclusivity of the underlying predicates. This establishes the semantic gap, but a second competent reading survives: since the model distinguishes the alternatives operationally via distinct event identities, this could be read as a design choice equivalent to disjointness in practice, even though the boolean predicates themselves are not proven exclusive. No predicate was available to resolve this ambiguity definitively (predicate_id=null), so the undercutting alternative remains a live, evidence-supported reading rather than defeated.
decisions.strongest_defeater: Because both events could in principle be raised simultaneously in the same step (both are independent boolean conditions, not modeled as mutually exclusive by construction), the trigger-based separation is a competent alternative reading that operationally distinguishes the alternatives by event identity even though no guard-level exclusivity proof exists.
